provenance: PR #41 R4, closing the half of T-R51 its own acceptance asked for and the labelling route did not ship. T-R51 said 'Watched red either way'. The route taken — CI's wall clocks are hand-read off the log of a named workflow run rather than committed to the ledger — landed with nothing that could go red, and ADR-019 §5 admitted it in those words: 'Nothing grades the four measurements'. Editing README's `74.04` to `99.99` left `--suite invariant` at 60/60 = 1.000. T-R51's own 'Compounding' clause was this same defect one version earlier: README published the CI band twice, in two incompatible forms (59.77 / 60.84 / 64.61 / 64.67s beside 69.37-74.06s), with 64.61 sitting in this repo's ledger as a LOCAL run — two documents drifting because one source was retyped into both. This gives the CI numbers the contract `published-band-matches-the-ledger` item 7 (readme-row) gives README's LOCAL band row — INCLUDING item 7's second half, the exactly-one-band-line rule from PR #35 R2/R4, which round 1 of this case claimed parity with and did not have (PR #41 R8): ADR-019 §5's attempt table is the ONE source, README's four `fast` values, both min-max ranges and the two CEILINGS THOSE RANGES DERIVE are read back FROM it rather than compared against literals typed into the check, README carries at most one CI band, the run id that makes them reader-checkable appears in both documents, and the ceilings §5 derives from its own maxima are the ones `.github/workflows/eval.yml` declares — which closes the chain table -> ADR-013's rule -> workflow, the thing the four numbers exist to justify. Deliberately NOT graded, because it cannot be from here: that anyone ever measured those four numbers. The run id is what a reader checks with `gh run view 32561162459 --attempt N --log`; this case only refuses the two documents drifting apart and a run id no document mentions. Same reason no CI row reaches the ledger (T-R73). The regexes are function-local rather than module-level because ADR-019 §6 enumerates the module-level names its band region does not pin, and a new constant there would have made that enumeration stale — the defect class §6 exists for.

triage.note: tagged invariant and fast, like the rest of the band/ceiling documentation guards. Pure code: three file reads and a few regexes, no network, no spend. It reads `.github/workflows/eval.yml`, which `fast-wall-clock-budget` also parses — that case pins the values the workflow declares, this one pins that those values are what ADR-019 §5's own table derives, so neither subsumes the other. What it does NOT cover, named rather than gestured at, because round 1's version of this note claimed a coverage it did not have (PR #41 R8): (1) whether the four measurements are real — unknowable locally, T-R73. (2) Any CI figure published outside ADR-019 §5 and README; ADR-013's copy of the superseded 95-case band is owned by `task/T-M32-9`. (3) The one-band rule reads a FORM — the bolded `**a / b / c / ds**` list — so a second band written unbolded is not seen. That is deliberate: README's superseded 95-case band is written exactly that way, unbolded and labelled superseded, and reddening on it would force the honest record out of the document. (4) Prose about CI that carries no number in a graded form at all.

(1) The reviewer's own: README's fourth `fast` value edited to `99.99` — {readme: fast_attempt_list_is_not_the_adr_table, expected: '69.37 / 69.54 / 74.04 / 74.06s'}. Before this case that same edit left `--suite invariant` at 60/60. (2) README's `invariant` range to `14.80-16.99s` — {readme: range_is_not_the_adr_table, suite: invariant, expected: '14.80-16.47s'}. (3) README's `fast` range to `69.37-74.60s` — the same key for `fast`. (4) The SOURCE edited instead of the copy: ADR-019 §5's attempt-2 `fast` cell to `76.06s`, leaving README stale — {expected: '69.37 / 69.54 / 74.04 / 76.06s'} plus {expected: '69.37-76.06s'}. That direction matters: the values are read back from the table, so the check follows the source rather than pinning a literal, and editing either side is red. (5) README's four mentions of the run id deleted — {readme: does_not_name_the_run_the_adr_cites, adr_cites: '32561162459'} — which is the T-R51 residue, a number a reader can no longer verify. Fixed to tolerate the wrap, the same allowance `_SIX_REF` already makes for slugs near a line end; had it been 'fixed' by relaxing what counts as a citation, it would have been a guard that stopped guarding. PR #41 R8 and R12 added five more, three of them against states this case was GREEN on when it shipped.
